title: PERFORM, in two minutes
description: A walkthrough of PERFORM: the named controls, what they turn, Wander, and the offer loop.

lines.text: PERFORM is where you play Auracle.
Everything in it is built for your hands, so nothing in it ever stops the music.
Play it from your computer keyboard, or plug in any MIDI controller.
The first eight knobs you turn claim the eight controls.
The six controls are named for what you hear: Bright, Snap, Motion, Body, Grit, and Space.
None of them is fixed to a knob. For each patch, Auracle measures what every knob does to the sound, and wires each control to the knobs that do the work.
Turn one, and the strip underneath shows the real knobs it's moving.
If a patch can't honestly do what a control says, the control turns amber. Turn it anyway, and Auracle adds what's missing, or grows a version that can.
The XY pad puts two controls under one finger.
Wander lets the model play along.
A little, and it offers ideas. More, and it drifts the knobs toward what you like. All the way, and it roams.
Press Offer, and a new version of what you're playing grows in slot B.
Hold Peek to hear it, or turn Blend to move between the two.
Take it, and it becomes your sound. Ask for another, and that's a pass.
Once you've heard an offer, either answer teaches the model what you like.
Keep marks where you are. Back returns to the last sound you kept.
That's the loop: play, turn, offer.
And the circuit is always one tab away, in PATCH.
